assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy is among the most consequential translational stories of recent decades: from hormone biology and the incretin effect to drugs that treat type 2 diabetes and obesity and show cardiovascular and renal benefit. The concept is clear, original and has changed clinical practice at very large scale.
assessment.attribution: Decisive contributions are spread across Holst (incretin physiology, GLP-1 as the active insulinotropic form), Drucker (GLP-1 biology, GLP-2, translational pharmacology) and Mojsov (peptide chemistry and identification of the active GLP-1 form). Knudsen (industrial development) is credited but would be a fourth name, and others such as Habener are outside the supplied credit; the three chosen names give the most defensible configuration but allocation of credit is disputed.
assessment.maturity: Strong, independent confirmation from many large outcome trials and widespread clinical use; timing is excellent because impact is now unmistakable.
uncertainties: Priority dispute around GLP-1(7-36) identification and peptide chemistry
Whether industrial drug development (Knudsen) should be recognised over basic discovery
Limit of three laureates excludes several key contributors

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells redirected against tumours with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new class of living drugs. The discovery is original, clinically transformative and conceptually clear.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain and June both developed second-generation costimulated CAR designs and led key clinical translation; Rosenberg pioneered adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T cells but his contribution is more of a foundational predecessor. Eshhar and others are not in the credited set. I propose June and Sadelain as the most direct pair.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent confirmation in leukaemia and lymphoma; effects in solid tumours remain limited, but the core discovery is mature and timely.
uncertainties: Credit relative to Rosenberg and the original CAR concept originators outside the credited set
Limited efficacy in solid tumours and toxicity/manufacturing issues
Whether recognition should treat cell therapy as a compound discovery

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotide correction of SMN2 exon 7 splicing led to nusinersen, the first effective disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, converting a lethal infantile disease into a treatable one. It is a clean example of mechanism-driven RNA therapeutics: from splicing regulation to a drug with dramatic clinical effect. I note my own field interest in RNA processing and have tried to weigh it on the merits using the common criteria.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and the antisense strategy for SMN2; Bennett led the development of the chemistry and clinical drug at Ibis. Other contributors (for example laboratory co-developers and clinical trial investigators) are outside the supplied credit. The two names support a coherent prize.
assessment.maturity: Approved in 2016, with large clinical datasets and independent follow-up confirming survival and motor benefit; the field has since expanded to other antisense drugs, which makes the timing mature.
uncertainties: Relationship to prior antisense chemistry recognised elsewhere
Allocation between mechanistic discovery and drug development
Variable response by treatment timing

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signalling logic in which ER stress is sensed and relayed to the nucleus, via Ire1, Hac1/XBP1 splicing and the UPR transcriptional programme. It is an original, basic discovery that clarified proteostasis and has implications for diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the clear core pair: Walter (Ire1 and the unconventional splicing pathway) and Mori (UPR elements and the transcriptional response). Cox and others contributed to the yeast pathway but are not in the credited set. The two-person configuration looks fair.
assessment.maturity: The pathway is well confirmed across species and conceptually stable; its extension into therapeutic benefit is still developing, but basic recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Therapeutic translation is still early
Contributions of other researchers such as Cox are not in the credited set

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR signalling established a central regulator linking nutrient and growth-factor signalling to cell growth, metabolism and ageing, with consequences for cancer, immunity and metabolic disease and clinical use of rapalogs. The discovery is original and broadly impactful.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR and its role in growth control; Sabatini identified mTOR-binding partners, mTORC1 regulation by amino acids and the Rag pathway. Schreiber contributed through rapamycin chemistry and FKBP12 work. I propose Hall and Sabatini, though the allocation of credit among Hall, Sabatini and Schreiber, and the roles of others such as Brown and Heitman, are not fully clear.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed over three decades and in clinic through rapamycin analogues, though the clinical impact is narrower than the basic biology implies.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Sabatini and Schreiber and others outside the credited set
Relative weight of Hall's yeast genetics versus Sabatini's mammalian mTORC1 work
Clinical benefit is narrower than the conceptual impact

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided cell-type-specific, millisecond-scale control of neural activity using microbial opsins, transforming experimental neuroscience and enabling causal circuit dissection across species. The invention is original, widely adopted and has recently begun to enter clinical translation (e.g. vision restoration).
assessment.attribution: Credit is crowded: Bamberg, Hegemann and Nagel discovered and characterised channelrhodopsin function; Boyden and Deisseroth demonstrated neuronal control; Miesenböck made earlier genetically targeted photo-activation. With a three-person limit I choose Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel, but the omission of Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck is a significant unresolved allocation issue.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature as a research tool with thousands of independent applications; clinical utility is still early, so it is timely as a tool but less so as medicine.
uncertainties: Strongly contested allocation among six credited names
Whether a tool/method fits the prize's discovery emphasis relative to a physiological or medical discovery
Clinical translation remains limited

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explains how cytosolic DNA is detected and converted to type I interferon and inflammatory responses, with implications for infection, autoimmunity, cancer immunity and ageing. It is a conceptually clean, mechanistically complete pathway.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP, and Barber identified STING; Ishikawa and the other authors contributed to STING identification. The Chen and Barber pair seems to capture the decisive contributions, with some uncertainty about the credit due to others.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely and mechanistically stable, but therapeutic validation (STING agonists and inhibitors) has not yet delivered an approved drug, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact not yet demonstrated
Credit to Ishikawa and others for STING versus Barber
Possible simultaneous discoveries and priority questions I cannot fully verify

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids rest on Lgr5 stem cell identification and culture conditions that let single stem cells self-organise into long-lived epithelial structures. Organoids have become a major platform for modelling disease, host-pathogen interactions and personalised medicine research.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem cell work and the organoid concept, with Sato performing the key culture development as first author. The pair is a reasonable configuration, although earlier contributors in 3D culture and the Lgr5 stem-cell concept may also deserve consideration.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and independently confirmed; clinical applications are still emerging, so the discovery is mature as a research method but its medical impact is still being established.
uncertainties: Medical impact is still emerging
Prior contributions in 3D culture and stem-cell biology outside the credited names
Methods-oriented discovery relative to prize emphasis
